title: Hosted Inference: Surface Simplification PRD, Scope Constraints, and Eval Gate Checklist
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: The hosted inference surface has accumulated feature permutations across chat/completions/embeddings/rerank that increase cognitive load for integrators, complicate testing, and inflate support overhead. This PRD narrows and simplifies the surface for the initial 2025.03 launch slice so we can provide a smaller, deterministic set of behaviors with clear eval gates and rollback criteria.

Goals: 1) Reduce surface area users must understand to integrate core capabilities (generate, chat, embed, rerank). 2) Provide deterministic fallback and degradation behavior with measurable signals. 3) Define acceptance gates tied to latency, error rates, and QA evals to prevent regressions. 4) Ship a launch checklist that operationalizes cutover, telemetry, alerts, and rollback runbooks.

Users: external customers integrating via REST/SDKs, internal FE/Docs, Solutions Engineers, and SRE on-call teams.

Background: Over the past 18 months we added optional parameters (prefill_kv, multi-lane routing, custom tokenization hints, ephemeral_kv toggles) that are valuable but rarely combined in customer usage. We will scope a minimal, opinionated surface for initial launch while preserving the ability to reintroduce advanced knobs behind feature flags and Dedicated plans.
scope:
In-scope for 2025.03 launch slice: 
- Canonical endpoints for: /v1/chat (conversational compose), /v1/completions (single-shot generate), /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank.
- A trimmed parameter set per endpoint (see Requirements).
- Deterministic fallback behavior when model variant unavailable (explicit mapping to fallback model set).
- Eval harness and curated prompt suite for each endpoint (functional and quality checks).
- Telemetry dashboards for per-route latency, 99th percentile tail, error budget burn, and per-model quality regression signals.
- Rollout canaries at 1%, 10%, 50%, 100% with automated rollback triggers.
out_of_scope:
- Advanced runtime knobs (manual batching config, kernel selection overrides) except behind internal feature flag.
- Dedicated-only capacity features (tenant burst pools, reserved routing).
- VPC/private-plane packaging.
- Multi-protocol (grpc) adapter for launch slice (returns to backlog).
requirements: 1) Each endpoint surface must accept a standardized request shape with explicit minimal fields: input, model (optional), max_tokens/limit where relevant, temperature/rank_beta where applicable, metadata for tracing. 2) Disable or hide legacy boolean toggles that cause non-deterministic outputs for launch (list of deprecated params in linked spec). 3) Provide documented deterministic fallback mapping table. 4) Latency SLO: p95 < 220ms for small gen (<=128 tokens), p95 < 450ms for medium gen (<=512 tokens) on standard hosted lane. 5) Error budget target: <0.5% 5xx on all endpoints during launch slice. 6) Eval harness: automated quality regression detection using a curated set of 600 prompts across gen/chat/embeddings/rerank with pass/fail thresholds defined below. 7) Canary rollout automation integrated with Console: canary slices, automatic metric collection, and auto-rollback if thresholds exceeded. 8) Developer docs and SDK snippet updates published before canary.
acceptance_criteria: API schema validated: JSON schema check + examples published in docs/hosted-surface-simplified.md
All deprecated/hidden params removed from the public docs and API surface for the launch slice
Eval harness green: pass rate >= 98% for embeddings similarity tests, >= 95% for generation relevance metrics, >= 97% for rerank NDCG@10 plateau compared to baseline model
Performance gates met in staging under synthetic load that mimics target production mix: p95 latency targets and 5xx error budget
Canary automation configured with roll-forward and roll-back triggers in Console (on-call runbook linked)
Telemetry dashboards live with historical baselines and alerting thresholds wired to PagerDuty
Security review completed with KMS integration checklist (if customer-supplied keys are allowed) and signed off by Security
SDK and quickstart templates updated in SDK repo and example apps exercise only the simplified surface
rollout_plan: Stage 1 - Staging: run eval harness with synthetic and replay traffic; measure SLOs and quality metrics. Stage 2 - Internal beta (10% internal traffic): surface exposed to Redwood integrations (internal apps) for two business days. Stage 3 - Public canary (1% external): accept external traffic slice for 24hrs; monitor. Stage 4 - Gradual ramp to 10% then 50% over 48hrs each with hold windows, then 100%. At each stage, automated checks evaluate latency charts, 5xx rates, and eval-harness snapshot. Immediate auto-rollback on any hard trigger (see rollout_steps_checklist).
rollout_steps_checklist: Create canary config in Console and assign model mapping
Deploy server changes to canary cluster
Run eval harness and commit report to QA dashboard
Enable 1% public canary and monitor 2x history window
Raise go/no-go sync with SRE, Product, and Docs owners
Ramp to 10% if green; hold 24hrs; re-evaluate metrics
Open rollout retrospective doc after 100% completion
test_plan:
- Unit tests for canonical request parsing and schema enforcement.
- Integration tests: end-to-end calls to /v1/chat, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank with mocked model backends and golden outputs.
- Quality tests: run eval harness nightly against canary and baseline snapshots.
- Load tests: replay product traffic mix to measure p95/p99 and KV cache hit behavior.
- Chaos tests: simulate model variant OOM and validate deterministic fallback path.
- Docs smoke tests: SDK snippets executed in CI to confirm examples compile and return expected shape.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-endpoint latency (p50/p95/p99), errors (4xx/5xx breakdown), throughput (requests/s), model fallback occurrences, quality-regression score (eval-harness drift). Alerts: - Major (PagerDuty): sustained 5xx rate > 0.5% for 10min or p95 latency > 2x baseline for 10min. - High (Slack + Oncall): quality-regression delta > threshold in consecutive nightly evals. - Medium (Slack): elevated fallback mapping events > 1% of traffic in 30min. All alerts must link to the runbook and a rollback toggle in Console.
decisions: Adopt a single canonical request envelope across endpoints to simplify SDKs (Decision 2025-01-20)
Hide advanced runtime knobs behind internal feature flags for launch slice (Decision 2025-01-22)
Use baseline-open-1 as the primary fallback model family for the initial rollout (Decision 2025-01-25)
risks: Quality regression: simplifying the surface may inadvertently remove subtle controls that customers rely on; mitigated by an eval suite and canary hold windows.
Support spike: customers using previously undocumented params will encounter breakage; mitigate with proactive docs/announcements and migration helper script.
SLA exposure: mis-tuned canary thresholds could cause noisy rollbacks; mitigate by conservative initial thresholds and a manual override path.
